Definition: from G1223 and a derivative of G2478; to stout it through, i.e. asservate:--confidently (constantly) affirm.
BiblicalUsage: To insist strongly, to affirm something with full confidence even when others doubt it. Rhoda insisted Peter really stood at the door, and another bystander insisted Peter was a follower of Jesus.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that some truths are worth insisting on even when the room disagrees, because confidence is not stubbornness when the fact is true.
